bigPicture: CoreWeave answered the report's two worries, demand and funding, in one night: backlog up to $132.5B and no new parent-level unsecured debt planned through 2027. That is why the leveraged AI names and chips lead.
The rate backdrop did not change: a December hike is now fully priced and 50 bp odds are 15%. Today's bounce is about AI funding, not about rates easing.
Money is rotating out of the defensives that led for a month (XLV -0.8%, XLP -0.5%, XLRE -0.3%) and into the beaten-down AI trade (SMH -17.8% over a month).
Nvidia is the exception to watch: it rises with the group (+3.9%) while carrying its own headline risk (Baird downgrade, Huang probe, earnings Nov 17).
snapshot.takeaway: CoreWeave fixed the funding scare for a day, but the Fed did not move: a December hike is fully priced. Gaps this size in names 15-35% below their averages can run or fade fast, so let the first 15 minutes show whether the premarket highs hold before trusting the bounce, and treat NVDA separately from the group.

sectors.text: CoreWeave beat on revenue, narrowed its loss, raised its 2026 revenue and operating income guide and said most 2027 needs come from customer prepayments and partner financing. NBIS +13.3% before its own report tomorrow, IREN +7.6%, ORCL +5.2%.

CoreWeave's $37-39B 2026 capex and 1.85 GW power target hold, and Talen (+5.8%) signed a 7-year, 750 MW capacity deal. VRT +6.1%. JPMorgan sees a possible AI rebound but stays cautious on electrical equipment.
The biggest premarket mover. SMH +4.8% after -6.7% over 5 days: MRVL +8.9%, MU +6.8%, LRCX +6.1%, AMD +5.8%, TSM +4.8%, AVGO +4.3%, NVDA +3.9%. UBS says AMD and Arm keep gaining server CPU share.
IGV +1.2% against XLK +2.7%. Microsoft (+0.4%) is still digesting Anthropic's Claude Sheets launch against Excel (I'm built by Anthropic). Software stays on the losing side of a hike in the report.
Brent 93.07 (+1.7%), WTI 87.22 (+1.4%) after reports of advanced Iranian plots against U.S. officials; Trump still cites 'positive momentum' and Iran denies talks. XLE +1.2% after -6.7% over 5 days.
